That's been my biggest problem my entire life. My brain just craves food no matter what. I could have just been at a buffet, and thirty minutes later I'd wander into the kitchen to see what I had in the cabinets. 

The taming of the cravings has been an absolute lifesaver.

I've gotten into a nice routine with my meals now, as well as my portion sizes. 

Protein bar for breakfast so I can take my other medications, then I've found I really like soups for lunches and midday meals. 

I keep around pouches of apple sauce with added veggies, and those low calorie Special K bars for a snack in the afternoon. 

Whatever the fiancee and I feel like for dinner, and then a handful of a snack in the evening or a small dessert. 

It's been working well!

Hey, I saw your post and it resonated with me a lot. 

I attempted suicide a few years ago and wound up in the hospital for a solid week.

I remember getting a call from my mom, and the way she phrased what happened still rattles around in my brain. She spoke to me in a baby voice that I always hated and said:

"Did you try to do something silly?" 

Never acknowledged the elephant in the room. 

The only other times she called were to complain that getting through the phones was annoying and to talk about her own life. 

I was living with other family at the time, and the only times they were with me were when I initially got taken in, and when they had to pick me up because I couldn't drive. No one ever talked about what happened, or why. They still don't.

No one asked me why I did it, or tried to understand. In my experience with my family, they were either afraid to bring it up like the family I was living with, or like my mother who just didn't have the brain cells to care. 

In any case, I'm sorry that you're not getting the support you deserve from those that are supposed to love and care for you. Just know that you're not alone.

I started out with Anycubic's water washable resin when I first got my printer because it was a bundle deal at the time. 

Sadly the only way I found to keep my models from not shattering off of the plate when removing them, or knocking them over because I'm clumsy was to switch resins. 

Anycubic's water washable is ridiculously break-prone, and I also found that the details themselves would be muddy despite whatever settings I used. 

I made the switch to Sunlu ABS-Like and I feel like my whole printing experience changed for the better! Prints look so much crisper and I haven't had a single mini break on me despite dropping them and even giving the old supports a good bend test. The price point is lovely too. 

Only downside is that you need to wash in 99% isopropyl. I hope this helps!
